title: Automating Human Tutor-Style Programming Feedback: Leveraging GPT-4 Tutor Model for Hint Generation and GPT-3.5 Student Model for Hint Validation
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of generating high-quality, human tutor-style programming feedback for students who submit buggy code. The authors focus on a practical challenge in programming education: large language models can generate feedback, but the quality is often below that of human tutors and not reliable enough for classroom deployment.

The proposed approach, GPT4Hints-GPT3.5Val, uses GPT-4 as a tutor model to generate hints and detailed explanations, augmented with symbolic information such as failing test cases and, when available, a fixed version of the program. A second stage uses GPT-3.5 as a student model to validate whether the explanation actually helps fix the bug, thereby trading off precision and coverage through repeated trials and threshold-based acceptance rules.

The evaluation is conducted on three real-world datasets of introductory Python programming bugs: basic algorithms, regular expressions, and data analysis. The paper reports that the combined generation-and-validation approach achieves precision near human tutor levels while retaining substantial coverage, and that using a weaker model as a simulated student can improve validation effectiveness. The work is positioned as a technique for programming education rather than a study of learners, and it concludes that symbolic prompting plus student-style validation can materially improve AI-generated feedback quality.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical benchmark study with human expert evaluation, but it is not an educational intervention trial with learners. The evidence is method evaluation on curated buggy-program datasets, so it provides useful but indirect evidence for classroom effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows potentially meaningful gains in automated feedback precision and coverage, but the measured outcomes are technical proxy metrics rather than direct student learning gains. Impact on education is therefore promising but unclear and not yet demonstrated at the learner level.

interventions.use_case: LLM-generated tutor-style programming feedback and hint validation for buggy Python code, using GPT-4 to generate explanations/hints and GPT-3.5 to validate hint quality before release

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that GPT4Hints-GPT3.5Val achieves high-precision automated feedback suitable for sharing while reducing the need for human tutor involvement. Across three Python programming datasets (total buggy programs n=79), the method reached about 95% precision with over 70% coverage in two of the three datasets, indicating strong potential to reduce tutor workload while maintaining quality.
finding.measure: Precision and coverage of accepted programming feedback/hints; human expert rubric (HOverall) for feedback quality
